title: Exclude a nontrivial isolated exact return on a viscosity interval
statement: For ordinary integrable scalar forcing g(t)F from zero in the invariant fundamental-shear subspace, exact physical velocity is x_lambda F with x_prime+lambda x=g and lambda=nu kappa^2. If x_lambda(T)=0 for EVERY lambda in a nonempty OPEN interval, then integral_0^T exp(lambda s)g(s)ds=0 there. This finite-interval Laplace transform is analytic; all derivatives at an interior lambda0 vanish. The finite signed measure exp(lambda0 s)g(s)ds therefore annihilates every polynomial; density in C[0,T] forces g=0 almost everywhere. Thus a nontrivial isolated scalar pulse cannot have exact zero terminal velocity throughout a viscosity interval. This does not exclude arbitrary nonlinear multi-field returns. Paid approximate returns remain allowed and are exactly what the inherited moment-cancelled pulse supplies.
